Systematically Attacking The Front Headl.overview: Gordon Ryan's front headlock system, eight volumes. Volume 1 covers key differences between wrestling and jiu-jitsu front headlocks. Volume 2 covers the front head-and-arm / chin strap (including countering a basic guard pull with a knee slide). Volume 3 covers the front chest lock (countering a guard pull). Volume 4 covers the types of guillotine. Volume 5 covers the anaconda and the guillotine / anaconda dilemma. Volume 6 covers go-behinds and their consequences in wrestling versus jiu-jitsu. Volumes 7 and 8 are rolls with commentary.
Systematically Attacking The Front Headl.for: No-gi grapplers who snap people down or face guard pullers.

Systematically Attacking the Guard 3.0 (.overview: Gordon Ryan's newest passing approach, 'inside camping' (staying inside the opponent's legs and breaking the guard down from close range), eight volumes. Volume 1 introduces it, with Roger Gracie's influence. Volume 2 covers entries against seated guard (hand fighting to the inside step). Volume 3 covers high-head inside camping and the three half guards. Volume 4 covers the shoulder pull versus the V grip, and countering the knee lever. Volume 5 covers the 'cranial shift' and forcing half guard when they extend their legs. Volume 6 covers low-head inside camping. Volume 7 covers the knee-elbow connection and knee slides when it breaks. Volume 8 is rolling. Note: volumes 2 to 8 of your copy are MPEG-TS video files with an .mp4 name; they play fine in VLC.
Systematically Attacking the Guard 3.0 (.for: No-gi passers who want a lower-risk, pressure-based passing game.

Systematically Attacking The Guillotine.overview: Gordon Ryan's guillotine system, eight volumes, organised by position. Volume 1 is the overview. Volume 2 covers guillotines from closed guard (including after a failed hip bump). Volume 3 covers guillotines from bottom open guard (the shoulder and hip rule). Volume 4 covers guillotines from top open guard ('footballing' the head). Volume 5 covers guillotines from side control and mount. Volume 6 covers guillotines from the front headlock (defensive hand positions). Volumes 7 and 8 are rolls with commentary.
Systematically Attacking The Guillotine.for: No-gi grapplers who want the guillotine from everywhere.
key: Guillotine from closed guard and hip bump
From open guard bottom and top

Systematically Attacking Triangles By Go.overview: Gordon Ryan's triangle system, eight volumes. Volume 1 covers triangle theory. Volume 2 covers triangles from supine guard (the clamp). Volume 3 covers triangles from pins (mount to front, back and wrong-way triangles). Volume 4 covers finishing mechanics for the front triangle. Volume 5 covers the wrong-way triangle (hantai sankaku). Volume 6 covers the side triangle (yoko sankaku). Volumes 7 and 8 are rolls with commentary.
Systematically Attacking Triangles By Go.for: No-gi grapplers who want triangles from bottom and top.
